# Name-overload report — range A (n = 0–24)

Rewrites follow "Short and memorable": sentences under ~12 words, ≤2 proper nouns per sentence, ≤3 per paragraph. Author block-0 lines (Queen Sunduk, Eight Great Clans, Gotaso, Yunchung, The Severing, Maehwa) are untouched.
**`at` note:** where a rewrite drops a phrase that an image's `at` hangs on, the line says so. Either keep that phrase or move the `at` in the same pass.

### Queen Sunduk (#0)
- **b3**: names: 4 (Chunchu, Samhan, Bupmin, Gotaso). Why it glazes: three people, three ages and a dashed aside, all in one sentence.
  - Before: "Meanwhile, her husband Chunchu (29) — already, in quieter rooms, the most cunning man in Samhan — and young son Bupmin (6) and daughter Gotaso (7) are preparing."
  - After (EN): "Her husband Chunchu is dressing too. He is twenty-nine, and already the most cunning man in Samhan. Only the quiet rooms know it yet. Their two children are getting under everyone's feet."
  - After (KO): "남편 춘추도 채비 중이다. 스물아홉, 벌써 삼한에서 가장 교활한 사내다. 아직은 조용한 방들만 그걸 안다. 두 아이는 어른들 발밑을 헤집고 다닌다."
  - Keeps the `at` "the most cunning man in Samhan". The children get their names in b4 and b8.
- **b14**: names: 7 (Bone, Rank, System, Common, Ranks, Nobles, Royals). Why it glazes: a capitalised textbook taxonomy plus a gloss (골품제), and b16 does the same job better with sleeves.
  - Before: "Silla is a class society dominated by the Bone Rank System (골품제), where everything is determined by one’s rank. There are the 6 Common Ranks, and then the Nobles and Royals."
  - After (EN): "Silla runs on bone. Your rank is your birth, and your birth is your life. Six common ranks at the bottom. Above them, the nobles. Above them, the royals."
  - After (KO): "신라는 뼈로 돌아간다. 골품이 곧 태생이고, 태생이 곧 평생이다. 맨 아래 여섯 두품. 그 위에 진골. 그 위에 성골."
  - You could also cut this block outright, since the b15 diagram and the b16 sleeves cover it.
- **b19**: names: 3 people plus "Royals" (Dukman, Seungman, Chunmyung). Why it glazes: a roll call with emoji and ages in parentheses.
  - Before: "There are now only 3 Royals left — 🌸 Princess Dukman (37), 🌼 Princess Seungman (32), and 🎖 Princess Chunmyung (52)."
  - After (EN): "Three royals are left. All three are the old king's daughters. Dukman, thirty-seven. Seungman, thirty-two. Chunmyung, fifty-two. That is the whole bloodline, and all of it is women."
  - After (KO): "남은 왕족은 셋. 셋 다 선왕의 딸이다. 덕만, 서른일곱. 승만, 서른둘. 천명, 쉰둘. 핏줄은 그게 전부고, 전부 여자다."
  - The `at` "There are now only 3 Royals left" is used by five images. Move it to "Three royals are left".
- **b23**: names: 4 (Sunduk, Blue Moon, Divine Country, Silla). Why it glazes: emoji, age, an epithet in dashes and a title, all in one line.
  - Before: "👑 Queen Sunduk (37) — the Blue Moon of the Divine Country — becomes the first Queen of Silla."
  - After (EN): "And so she becomes the first Queen of Silla. They will call her Queen Sunduk, the Blue Moon of the Divine Country."
  - After (KO): "그렇게 그녀는 신라의 첫 여왕이 된다. 사람들은 그녀를 선덕여왕, 신국의 푸른 달이라 부를 것이다."
  - Keeps both `at`s ("becomes the first Queen of Silla" and "the Blue Moon of the Divine Country").
- **b26**: names: 7 (Yushin, Sword of Silla, Munhee, Dukman, Hwarang, Surabol). Why it glazes: a file-card introduction stacking age, epithet, kinship, rumour and job description.
  - Before: "Marshal Yushin (37), Sword of Silla, Munhee’s older brother, is unusually close with Princess Dukman. He is the leader of the Hwarang, an elite training corps for young noblemen — horse, bow, and the gyuku field where…"
  - After (EN): "Munhee's big brother is Yushin. He is thirty-seven, and he runs the yard. Horse, bow, gyuku: that is where boys learn whether they matter. People call him the Sword of Silla. He is also, everyone notices, very fond of the princess."
  - After (KO): "문희의 오라버니는 유신이다. 서른일곱, 연무장의 주인이다. 말, 활, 격구. 소년들은 거기서 제가 중요한 사람인지 배운다. 사람들은 그를 신라의 도검이라 부른다. 그리고 다들 눈치챘듯, 공주를 유난히 아낀다."
  - Two images (`yushin-chunchu-munhee`, `scene-yushin-chunchu-bad-boy-5`) hang on "Sword of Silla, Munhee’s older brother", and one hangs on "Marshal Yushin (37)". Move them.
- **b45**: names: 5 (Hwarang, Bidam, Second Blade, Alchun, Pumsuk). Why it glazes: a roll call with colour emoji, and an appositive nested inside the list.
  - Before: "The young Hwarang knights, including 🟣 Bidam (38) — already the Second Blade in the yard’s private ledger — 🟡 Alchun (36), and 🟢 Pumsuk (14), pledge allegiance to the throne."
  - After (EN): "Then the young knights kneel and pledge themselves to the throne. Bidam kneels in front, already the yard's Second Blade. Pumsuk is fourteen, and trying very hard not to look it."
  - After (KO): "젊은 화랑들이 무릎 꿇고 왕좌에 충성을 맹세한다. 맨 앞은 비담, 연무장 장부에선 벌써 제이검이다. 품석은 열넷이고, 열넷처럼 안 보이려고 무진 애를 쓴다."
  - Alchun doesn't need this introduction, because he speaks in b17 and b57.

### Harmony Council (#1)
- **b1**: names: 2 plus a gloss (Harmony Council, 화백회의, Nobles). Why it glazes: the first narration line is a gloss and a civics definition.
  - Before: "The Harmony Council (화백회의), the ruling body of Nobles, debate who the next king should be."
  - After (EN): "The Harmony Council meets to debate who the next king should be. Six nobles, one night. Nobody stands up until they all agree."
  - After (KO): "화백회의가 다음 왕을 누구로 할지 논한다. 귀족 여섯, 밤 하나. 뜻이 하나로 모이기 전엔 아무도 일어서지 못한다."
  - Keeps the `at` "debate who the next king should be".
- **b11 (flashback, inner p0)**: names: 4 (Chunchu, Kim Yongsu, Council, Surabol). Why it glazes: the father arrives with his whole genealogy and a rumour in one sentence.
  - Before: "Chunchu is nine. His father wakes him past midnight, which is not unusual, and walks him down to the stream below the palace, which is. Kim Yongsu is the son of the king the Council unmade, and Surabol has a word…"
  - After (EN): "Chunchu is nine. His father wakes him past midnight, which is normal, and walks him to the stream below the palace, which isn't. Kim Yongsu is the son of a king the Council threw out. The capital has a word for him that it only says after he leaves. He talks to the dark. He laughs a beat late. He adds a granary ledger faster than the clerk can read it."
  - After (KO): "춘추는 아홉 살이다. 자정 넘어 아버지가 그를 깨우는 건 흔한 일이고, 궁 아래 개울로 데려가는 건 흔치 않다. 김용수는 화백이 끌어내린 왕의 아들이다. 도성엔 그가 방을 나간 뒤에만 쓰는 말이 있다. 그는 어둠에 대고 말한다. 한 박자 늦게 웃는다. 곳간 장부는 서기가 읽는 것보다 빨리 머릿속으로 더한다."
- **b25**: names: 9 (Sword of Silla, Kim Yushin, Second Blade, Bidam, Gaya-blood, Surabol, Hwarang). Why it glazes: two epithets and a two-family genealogy are wedged between four dashes around two names.
  - Before: "Across the floor the Sword of Silla — Kim Yushin — catches the Second Blade’s eye — Bidam — Gaya-blood marshal’s grandson and the boy from one of Surabol’s oldest halls, trading wins since they were Hwarang…"
  - After (EN): "Across the floor, Yushin catches the Second Blade's eye. He and Bidam have been trading wins since they were boys in the yard. The count stands at one hundred and eight apiece. Neither lets the other stay ahead for long."
  - After (KO): "마루 건너, 유신이 제이검과 눈을 맞춘다. 그와 비담은 연무장 소년 시절부터 승패를 주고받아 왔다. 수는 백팔 대 백팔. 어느 쪽도 상대를 오래 앞서 두지 않는다."
  - Keeps the `at`s "Across the floor" and "catches the Second Blade". The Gaya-grandson detail already lands in *Chunchu & Munhee* b42.

### Jinheung, the Cloud (#2)
- **b0**: names: 10 (Battle of Gwansanseong, Silla, Seong, Baekje, Han River, Goguryeo, Cloud King, Jinheung). Why it glazes: a battle name, a gloss, a year, two regnal numbers and a backstory clause come before any person. It also spends the death that *The Severing* (#18) dramatizes, so the event gets told twice.
  - Before: "At the Battle of Gwansanseong (관산성) in 554, Silla’s armies kill King Seong (#26) of Baekje — the man who had, only a year before, helped Silla take the Han River from Goguryeo. The man who orders…"
  - After (EN): "Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they'll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they'll change the subject. You'll find out why. Not yet."
  - After (KO): "서라벌 사람에게 구름왕을 물으면 그의 비석 이야기를 할 것이다. 사비 사람에게 물으면 말을 돌릴 것이다. 왜인지는 알게 된다. 아직은 아니다."
  - This is the rule file's own GOOD example, and it belongs here. The `at` "The man who orders that killing is" (two images) needs to move to "Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King".
- **b1**: names: 6 (Silla, Han River, Malgal, Gaya, Samhan). Why it glazes: reign arithmetic and a territory list.
  - Before: "He took the throne at seven and reigned thirty-six years. By the end of them Silla held the Han River basin, the east coast up toward the Malgal country, and Gaya. He got there by being…"
  - After (EN): "He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. By the end, Silla had a river, a coastline and Gaya. He got there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he wasn't."
  - After (KO): "왕관을 쓸 때 그는 일곱 살이었다. 왕관은 너무 컸고, 아무도 그 말을 하지 않았다. 마지막엔 신라가 강 하나, 해안 하나, 그리고 가야를 쥐고 있었다. 그는 삼한에서 가장 믿을 만한 동맹이라서 거기까지 갔다. 믿을 수 없게 된 그 오후까지는."
- **b5**: names: 2 plus a five-verb list (Hwarang, Flowering Knights). Why it glazes: a gloss by apposition, then a list of five verbs.
  - Before: "Later in his reign he formalises the Hwarang, the Flowering Knights — a youth corps of noble boys who train together, travel together, sing together, die together, and measure one another…"
  - After (EN): "Late in his reign he invents the Hwarang. Take the noblest boys and put them in one yard. Make them ride, sing and rank each other until the ranking feels like fate. Nearly every man who matters later comes out of that yard."
  - After (KO): "말년에 그는 화랑을 만든다. 가장 귀한 집 소년들을 한 마당에 모은다. 말 타고 노래하고 서로 순위를 매기게 한다. 순위가 운명처럼 느껴질 때까지. 훗날 중요해지는 사내는 거의 다 그 마당에서 나온다."
- **b6**: names: 2 (Hwarang, Marshal). Why it glazes: an org chart ("six Hwarang under a Marshal, four disciples under each") that the b7 diagram repeats.
  - Before: "The yard is an officer factory: one class a year, six Hwarang under a Marshal, four disciples under each. The number is kept for life…"
  - After (EN): "One class a year. The number sticks to a man for life. Almost every sleeve on the Council first slept in that hall."
  - After (KO): "한 해에 한 기수. 그 숫자는 평생 따라다닌다. 화백의 소매들은 거의 다 그 방에서 처음 잤다."
- **b9**: names: 2 plus hanja (Beopun, 法雲). Why it glazes: a hanja gloss in the middle of the best joke in the entry.
  - Before: "Near the end he shaved his head. The king who had put stones on four mountains put on a monk’s robe instead and took the name Beopun (法雲, Dharma Cloud)…"
  - After (EN): "Near the end he shaved his head. The king of the four mountain stones put on a monk's robe and took a new name: Dharma Cloud. His queen went into a nunnery beside him. The court kept calling him Majesty. He kept answering to the other thing."
  - After (KO): "말년에 그는 머리를 깎았다. 네 산에 비석을 세운 왕이 승복을 입고 새 이름을 받았다. 법운. 법의 구름. 왕비도 그 곁 절로 들어갔다. 조정은 계속 전하라 불렀다. 그는 계속 다른 이름에 대답했다."

### Prince Euija (#3)
- **b0**: names: 4 plus a year (King Mu, Sabi, Euija, Baekje). Why it glazes: the opening line is a date and a title chain.
  - Before: "In the spring of 632 King Mu does at last what Sabi has been betting on for years, and names his eldest son Prince Euija (32) Crown Prince of Baekje. Thirty-two is late for it…"
  - After (EN): "Thirty-two is late to be named crown prince. By the time his father gets around to it, Euija has more than fifteen sons. The clans have had years to decide which ones they own."
  - After (KO): "서른둘이면 태자 책봉으로는 늦다. 아버지가 겨우 결심했을 때, 의자에겐 이미 아들이 열다섯 넘게 있다. 가문들은 그중 누구를 제 것으로 할지 정할 시간이 넉넉했다."
- **b5**: names: 5 (Yung, Tae, Hyo, Yun, Pung). Why it glazes: five names with ages, and three of those boys never matter.
  - Before: "The young princes — Yung (17), Tae (16), Hyo (15), Yun (12), and Pung (8) — grow up already spoken for: each with a clan’s ring on his finger…"
  - After (EN): "The young princes grow up already spoken for. Yung is the eldest. Pung is eight and has good handwriting. Each boy wears a clan's ring, hears a clan's tutor, and finds a clan's grudge folded into his allowance."
  - After (KO): "어린 왕자들은 자라기도 전에 임자가 정해져 있다. 맏이는 융. 여덟 살 풍은 글씨를 잘 쓴다. 저마다 가문의 반지를 끼고, 가문의 스승 말을 듣고, 용돈엔 가문의 원한이 접혀 들어 있다."
  - "Good handwriting" plants *King Euija* b58. Keeps the `at` "grow up already spoken for".

### Eight Great Clans (#4)
- **b1**: names: 5 plus a gloss (Eight Great Clans, 대성팔족, Baekje, Satek, Yunbi, Assembly). Why it glazes: right after Heewon's list line, the narrator glosses it and adds a governance note.
  - Before: "Baekje is dominated by the Eight Great Clans (대성팔족) — eight houses, eight fighting styles, one king between them. Satek fights with the king’s sleeve; Yunbi fights with the coast road…"
  - After (EN): "The Eight Great Clans run this country, and one king sits between them. Satek fights with the king's sleeve. Yunbi fights with the coast road. The other six keep their techniques quiet."
  - After (KO): "여덟 대성이 이 나라를 쥐고, 그 사이에 왕 하나가 앉아 있다. 사택은 왕의 소매로 싸운다. 연비는 해안 길로 싸운다. 나머지 여섯은 제 수법을 입 밖에 내지 않는다."
  - Keeps the `at` "The Eight Great Clans".
- **b3**: names: 2 (Sabi, west bridge). Why it glazes: four stacked clauses and a long dashed aside before anything moves, and "Eight houses. Eight fighting styles." repeats b1.
  - Before: "Once a year the street volume drops and the palace raises its own. On the packed earth inside the Sabi halls the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard — four hard lines, no furniture…"
  - After (EN): "Once a year, the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard. Four hard lines. No banners. The young men of each house step onto the grid in white. It's the same quarrel as the west bridge, only without the carts."
  - After (KO): "해마다 한 번, 궁은 마당에 네모난 격자를 분필로 긋는다. 단단한 선 넷. 깃발은 없다. 각 가문의 젊은이들이 흰옷을 입고 격자에 오른다. 서쪽 다리에서 하던 그 싸움이다. 수레만 없을 뿐."
  - Keeps the `at`s "square grid in the palace yard" and "young men of each house step onto the gr…".
- **b6**: names: 4 (Mokgeom, Jinmo, Sangdanse, Satek). Why it glazes: this is a shot list in narration ("Mokgeom mid-strike on the grid… Over his shoulder the chalk holds… the hard L of the square") with untranslated technique names.
  - Before: "The sword bouts go first. Mokgeom — wood that still remembers steel. A boy from Jinmo takes Sangdanse high guard; a Satek answers from middle. On the call they move: overhead cut…"
  - After (EN): "Swords first. Wooden ones, which still remember steel. A Jinmo boy holds his blade high. A Satek boy answers from the middle. On the call they both move. Blades skim the chalk. The white sleeves clap together so close that the steps gasp."
  - After (KO): "칼부터. 목검이다. 아직 쇠를 기억하는 나무. 진모 소년이 칼을 높이 든다. 사택 소년은 중단에서 받는다. 구령이 떨어지자 둘이 동시에 움직인다. 칼날이 분필 위를 스친다. 흰 소매가 맞부딪는 소리에 계단이 숨을 삼킨다."
  - Keeps "Blades skim the chalk." Move the `at`s "Mokgeom mid-strike on the grid" and "Over his shoulder the chalk holds" to "Wooden ones, which still remember steel" and "The white sleeves clap together".
- **b9** (and b8): names: 3 plus terms (Hae, Guk, deulbaejigi; satba in b8). Why it glazes: a wrestling manual, with a technique name and a three-step lift sequence, instead of a moment.
  - Before: "A Hae youth hooks; a Guk answers with hip. Then deulbaejigi clears the sand — lift onto the belly, second hoist, turn right, and the other man’s feet leave the earth…"
  - After (EN): "A Hae boy hooks a leg. A Guk boy answers with his hip. He lifts, he turns, and the other boy's feet leave the earth. The yard goes quiet the way a dock goes quiet when a rope snaps. Sand takes the shoulder. The chalk does not argue."
  - After (KO): "해 소년이 다리를 건다. 국 소년이 엉덩이로 받는다. 들어 올리고, 돌리고, 상대의 발이 땅을 떠난다. 밧줄 끊긴 부두처럼 마당이 조용해진다. 모래가 어깨를 받는다. 분필은 따지지 않는다."
  - Keeps "Sand takes the shoulder." Move the `at` "deulbaejigi clears the sand" to "the other boy's feet leave the earth". In b8, drop "satba" and keep "The bout is the hold."
- **b12**: names: 0 (it's a structure problem). Why it glazes: it repeats the elders-miscount line from the b11 dialogue word for word, then decodes the scene ("That was never the point. The point was…").
  - Before: "From the timber steps the houses keep score like berths. The elders watch from the hall steps — always — and still miscount when the sleeve is theirs. By dusk the white is grey…"
  - After (EN): "By dusk the white is grey with chalk and grit. Nobody has settled four generations of anything. The throne likes it that way. The boys go home with a score instead of a funeral."
  - After (KO): "해 질 녘, 흰옷은 분필과 모래로 잿빛이 된다. 사대에 걸친 무엇 하나 결판나지 않았다. 왕좌는 그게 좋다. 소년들은 장례 대신 점수를 들고 집에 간다."
  - The `at` "elders watch from the hall steps" lives in b11 dialogue, so moving it is safe.
- **b18**: names: 2 plus a gloss (Ministers’ Assembly, 정사암회의). Why it glazes: a gloss, and "fifty-odd sons" re-counts the herald joke.
  - Before: "They fight for power in the Ministers’ Assembly (정사암회의), each house controlling a share of the king’s fifty-odd sons…"
  - After (EN): "In the Assembly they fight for power, each house holding a share of the king's sons. They fight in the street too. Same fight. The street version is older."
  - After (KO): "회의에서 그들은 권력을 두고 싸운다. 가문마다 왕의 아들 몇씩을 쥐고서. 거리에서도 싸운다. 같은 싸움이다. 거리 쪽이 더 오래됐다."
- **b22**: names: 6 (Assembly, White River, Tamla, Yamato, Baekje). Why it glazes: four sentences that read like a cargo manifest.
  - Before: "What the Assembly votes on, more often than war, is water. Who may load first at the western wharves. Whose ships may winter in the White River mouth. Which house takes the Tamla orange levy…"
  - After (EN): "What the Assembly votes on, more often than war, is water. Who loads first. Whose ships winter in the river mouth. Who gets the orange levy, and who gets the silk berth. In this country, a clan without a harbour can't feed a fight."
  - After (KO): "회의가 전쟁보다 자주 표결하는 건 물이다. 누가 먼저 싣는가. 누구 배가 강어귀에서 겨울을 나는가. 귤 공물은 누가, 비단 선석은 누가 갖는가. 이 나라에서 항구 없는 가문은 싸움을 먹여 살리지 못한다."
- **b34**: names: 3 (Assembly, Elder Satek, Yunbi). Why it glazes: a seven-sentence anecdote whose tense slips from past to present in the last line.
  - Before: "Once, a grain levy that both houses had privately agreed to kill was brought to the Assembly anyway — a test, or a trap, or both. The votes lined up as everyone had counted…"
  - After (EN): "Once, both houses secretly agreed to kill a grain levy. It came to the Assembly anyway. The votes lined up as counted. Then Elder Satek, who had nodded all morning, turned his thumb down at the last call. The levy died. Yunbi's men stared. His own men stared harder. He never explained."

  - After (KO): "즉위 잔치에서 왕자들은 나이순으로 앉고, 상을 두 번이나 늘려야 한다. 왕 바로 옆엔 융, 그 곁엔 사택의 술 시중. 형제들 의자 뒤마다 가문의 스승이 두 번째 그림자처럼 서 있다. 저 끝에선 아직 새길 만한 이름도 없는 아이들에게 시종들이 술을 따른다."
  - Keeps the `at` "lengthened twice".
- **b62**: names: 3 (Chang’an, Baekje, Pung). Why it glazes: it spoils Baekje's fall in passing by saying his father becomes a prisoner in Chang’an.
  - Before: "Twenty years later his father is a prisoner in Chang’an and Baekje sends for him after all. Nobody at the feast would have believed it, Pung least of all."
  - After (EN): "One day Baekje will send for him after all. Nobody at the feast would have believed it, Pung least of all."
  - After (KO): "언젠가 백제는 결국 그를 부르러 사람을 보낸다. 잔치에 있던 누구도 믿지 않았을 것이다. 풍 자신이 가장."

### Yunchung (#17)
- **b10**: names: 5 (Ministers’ Assembly, Daeya, Satek, Yamato, Gyebek). Why it glazes: a writ, an inheritance case, three commodities and a sea route, all in one sentence.
  - Before: "In the Ministers’ Assembly that winter the loud fight is not yet Daeya but the southern shipping writ — who inherits it when a Satek cousin dies without a son; salt, iron, and the Yamato run…"
  - After (EN): "That winter, the Assembly's loud fight isn't about war. It's about a shipping writ. A Satek cousin has died without a son, and somebody has to inherit the salt, the iron and the run to the islands. Gyebek sits through three sessions. He understands every number and none of the smiles."
  - After (KO): "그해 겨울 회의의 큰 싸움은 전쟁이 아니다. 뱃길 문서다. 사택 집안 사촌 하나가 아들 없이 죽었고, 누군가는 소금과 쇠와 섬으로 가는 뱃길을 물려받아야 한다. 계백은 세 번의 회의를 내리 앉아 듣는다. 숫자는 전부 알아듣고, 웃음은 하나도 못 알아듣는다."
- **b14**: names: 2 plus an age (Euija, Divine Country). Why it glazes: a textbook headline ("makes plans to invade") for a decision the scene already made in b6–b9.
  - Before: "King Euija (41) makes plans to invade the Divine Country."
  - After (EN): "Euija has already decided. Now the clans have to believe it was their idea."
  - After (KO): "의자는 이미 정했다. 이제 가문들이 그게 제 생각이었다고 믿게만 하면 된다."

### The Severing (#18)
- **b1**: names: 9 plus a year (Baekje, Seong, Silla, Jinheung, Cloud King, Gaya, Goguryeo, Han River). Why it glazes: it opens on a year and a coalition roster, and the deal reads like a treaty summary.
  - Before: "In 551, Baekje under King Seong and Silla under Jinheung — the Cloud King — with Gaya contingents — push Goguryeo out of the Han River basin. The understanding is clear enough for wartime…"
  - After (EN, split into two `p`): "Two kings take a river back together. One is Seong of Baekje. The other is the Cloud King." / "The deal is simple. Baekje gets the river mouth, near the sea. Silla gets the upper valley. For two years, everybody keeps it."
  - After (KO): "두 왕이 함께 강을 되찾는다. 하나는 백제의 성왕. 다른 하나는 구름왕이다." / "약속은 간단하다. 바다 가까운 하류는 백제가, 위쪽 골짜기는 신라가. 두 해 동안은 모두 그 약속을 지킨다."
- **b2**: names: 5 plus two glosses and a year (Dokseongsanseong, Cloud King, Baekje, Han, Sinju). Why it glazes: two Korean glosses for places the reader never needs.
  - Before: "At Dokseongsanseong (독산성) and along the river the allied banners still fly together. Then, in 553, the Cloud King turns his army on the Baekje share. He seizes the lower Han, installs a new province — Sinju (신주)…"
  - After (EN): "For a while the two banners still fly side by side. Then the Cloud King turns his army on Baekje's half. He takes the river mouth and gives it a new name. He fills it with men who won't ask what the alliance meant."
  - After (KO): "한동안 두 나라 깃발은 여전히 나란히 나부낀다. 그러다 구름왕이 백제 몫으로 군대를 돌린다. 하류를 빼앗아 새 이름을 붙인다. 동맹이 무엇이었는지 묻지 않을 사람들로 그곳을 채운다."
  - Keeps the `at` "the Cloud King turns his army".
- **b3**: names: 7 plus a year (Seong, Baekje, Gaya, Wa, Yamato, Gwansanseong, Silla). Why it glazes: a muster roll and a fortress name with a year.
  - Before: "King Seong feels the cut in the marrow. He gathers Baekje, remaining Gaya houses, and a Wa contingent promised by the Yamato court, and in 554 marches on Gwansanseong…"
  - After (EN): "King Seong feels the cut in the marrow. He calls in everyone who still owes him: the last Gaya houses, a boatload of soldiers from the islands. Then he marches on the fortress that opens Silla's throat."
  - After (KO): "성왕은 그 칼날을 골수로 느낀다. 아직 그에게 빚진 이들을 모두 불러 모은다. 가야의 남은 집안들, 섬나라에서 건너온 군사들. 그리고 신라의 목을 여는 성으로 진군한다."
  - Keeps "King Seong feels the cut in the marrow". Move the `at` "He gathers Baekje, remaining Gaya houses" (`gwansan-three-hosts`) to "He calls in everyone who still owes him".
- **b5**: names: 4 plus a gloss (Yochang, Wideok, Seong, Gucheon). Why it glazes: a future regnal name in parentheses and a place gloss.
  - Before: "For months the fight goes Baekje’s way. Crown Prince Yochang (later King Wideok) holds the forward camp half-starved. Seong rides out at night with a small escort — fifty horse, the records say — to steady his son at Gucheon (구천)."
  - After (EN): "For months the fight goes Baekje's way. The crown prince holds the forward camp, half-starved. One night his father rides out with fifty horse to steady him."
  - After (KO): "몇 달 동안 싸움은 백제 쪽으로 기운다. 태자는 굶주리며 앞 진영을 지킨다. 어느 밤, 아버지가 기병 쉰을 이끌고 아들을 다독이러 나간다."
- **b9**: names: 6 (Kim Muryuk, Sinju, Geumgwan, Silla, Gaya, Muryuk). Why it glazes: **it opens the mystery box.** It names Muryuk before his own episode and stacks three offices in one appositive.
  - Before: "Kim Muryuk is already down in the cut — military governor of the new Sinju, a prince of fallen Geumgwan, Silla’s commission over a Gaya cone. Muryuk’s cone cuts the night ridge. He does not draw. He watches."
  - After (EN): "A man in a Gaya cone helm is already down in the cut. He wears Silla's commission over it. His cone cuts the night ridge. He does not draw. He watches."
  - After (KO): "가야의 고깔 투구를 쓴 사내가 이미 패인 길 아래에 있다. 그 위에 신라의 임명을 걸쳤다. 그의 고깔이 밤 능선을 가른다. 그는 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 본다."
  - Move the `at` "Muryuk’s cone cuts the night ridge" to "His cone cuts the night ridge". The dialogue in b10–b11 ("A prince of Geumgwan" / "Military governor of Sinju") also nearly answers the box. Consider "Gaya…? On this road, tonight. Why." / "Sit."

### Siege of Daeya (#21)
- **b38**: names: 8 (Surabol, Blue Moon, Sunduk, Seungman, Chunmyung, Munhee, Chunchu, Bupmin). Why it glazes: a chain of glances through six people in one sentence. It also sits *between* Pumsuk's surrender lines (b37, b39), so the news reaches Surabol before the fortress has fallen.
  - Before: "A messenger brings the news to Surabol. The Blue Moon — Queen Sunduk — receives it seated, because queens receive everything seated. Seungman covers her mouth. Chunmyung looks at Munhee, who is already looking at Chunchu…"
  - After (EN): "A messenger brings the news home. The Queen receives it seated, because queens receive everything seated. Munhee is already looking at Chunchu. Chunchu is looking at nothing at all. Bupmin asks the messenger to say it again, in the voice of a boy who thinks a sentence can be wrong twice."
  - After (KO): "전령이 소식을 들고 온다. 여왕은 앉은 채로 받는다. 여왕은 무엇이든 앉아서 받으니까. 문희는 벌써 춘추를 보고 있다. 춘추는 아무것도 보지 않는다. 법민이 전령에게 다시 말해 보라고 한다. 같은 문장이 두 번은 틀릴 수 있다고 믿는 소년의 목소리로."
  - Move this block after b44/b45 (Jukjuk), just before the herald line b41.

### Supreme Commander (#22)
- **b0**: names: 6 (Yeon Taejo, Eastern Command, Summit, Yeon, Eastern Commander, Youngryu). Why it glazes: a death, an inheritance, a committee, a banquet and a guest list in four long sentences.
  - Before: "Yeon Taejo dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The Eastern Command is his son’s by blood and by a decade of doing the work, and the Summit takes the whole summer to admit it…"
  - After (EN): "Yeon's father dies in the spring, in his own bed in the east. The seal should pass to the son. The Summit takes the whole summer to admit it. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet. The king is in attendance."
  - After (KO): "봄에 연의 아버지가 동쪽 제 집 자리에서 숨을 거둔다. 인장은 아들에게 가야 마땅하다. 제가회의는 그걸 인정하는 데 여름 한 철을 다 쓴다. 마침내 인정하자, 연은 연회를 열기로 한다. 왕도 자리한다."
  - Keeps the `at`s "dies in the spring, in his own bed", "decides to host a banquet" and "is in attendance."
- **b10 / b14 / b18**: names: Son Daeha, Go Ul, Go Heumsong. Why it glazes: three new full names that arrive in the same breath they die. Yeon already says each one aloud in the dialogue, so the narration can drop them.
  - Before (b10): "First the Southern Commander — Son Daeha, who wanted the next levy for Yushin’s passes and called Eastern fighting easy work."
  - After (EN): "First the Southern Commander, who wanted the next levy for Yushin's passes and called Eastern fighting easy work." Do the same for b14 ("Then the Northern Commander, who would not freeze another winter…") and b18 ("The Western Commander had warned…").
  - After (KO): "먼저 남부 대가. 유신의 고개를 막겠다며 다음 징발을 달라던, 동부의 싸움은 쉬운 일이라던 자." Do the same for b14 and b18.
- **b26**: names: 3 (Yeon Gusesa, Central Commander, Summit). Why it glazes: an office string after the name.
  - Before: "Last of the banners: Yeon Gusesa, Central Commander, elder of the house — the soft voice that told a nephew to sit down because the Summit does not run on prophecies."
  - After (EN): "Last of the banners: his uncle. The soft voice that told a nephew to sit down, because the Summit does not run on prophecies."
  - After (KO): "깃발의 마지막은 숙부다. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌아가지 않는다며 조카에게 앉으라 하던, 그 부드러운 목소리."
  - Keeps the `at` "Summit does not run on prophecies".

### Chunchu & Yeon (#23)
- **b51**: names: 8 (Bojang, Mangniji, Mamok Pass, Jungnyeong, Goguryeo, Chunchu, Seon Dohae). Why it glazes: two pass names and four people in a paragraph whose point is a fake promise.
  - Before: "The letter goes to King Bojang rather than the Mangniji. Mamok Pass and Jungnyeong were Goguryeo’s land to begin with, it says, and once Chunchu is home he will ask his own sovereign to give them back…"

He signs with a flourish. He has no intention of doing any such thing. His drinking partner, finishing the jar, has no intention of mentioning it."
  - After (KO): "편지는 막리지가 아니라 왕에게 간다. 그 고개들은 본래 고구려 땅이니, 돌아가면 제 임금께 돌려드리라 청하겠다고 적혀 있다. 춘추는 멋들어지게 서명한다. 그럴 생각은 털끝만큼도 없다. 술단지를 비우던 술친구도 그 말을 꺼낼 생각이 털끝만큼도 없다."
  - Move the `at` "The letter goes to King Bojang rather th" (`bojang-samjogo-letter`) to "The letter goes to the king".

### Euija & Yeon (#24)
- **b14 (flashback "Hansung", inner p0; listed as b0 in audit-names)**: names: 6 plus regnal numbers (Siege of Hansung, Goguryeo, Jangsu, Baekje, Gaero). Why it glazes: the whole flashback is one bare chronicle line with two regnal numbers.
  - Before: "At the Siege of Hansung, Goguryeo’s King Jangsu (#20) kills Baekje’s King Gaero (#21)."
  - After (EN): "Once, a Goguryeo king came south and took Baekje's old capital. The Baekje king's head ended up on a Goguryeo wall. Baekje has not forgotten. Goguryeo has not apologised."
  - After (KO): "한때 고구려 왕이 남으로 내려와 백제의 옛 도읍을 빼앗았다. 백제 왕의 머리는 고구려 성벽에 걸렸다. 백제는 잊지 않았다. 고구려는 사과하지 않았다."

---

## The 5 worst paragraphs in this range
1. **Commander Yeon b5**: 11 names in one 70-word sentence. The Thousand-Li Wall lecture is the rule file's own BAD example.
2. **Jinheung, the Cloud b0**: 10 names, a gloss, a year and two regnal numbers. It also spends the death that *The Severing* dramatizes.
3. **Siege of Daeya b38**: eight people in a chain of glances, and the block sits in the wrong place in the timeline.
4. **Harmony Council b25**: two epithets and two genealogies inside four dashes, around a moment that should be one look across the floor.
5. **Grand Academy b6**: a regnal-year founding date, a foreign dynasty and a gloss, all before the scene starts.

The worst rule breach that isn't about name count is **The Severing b9**, which names Muryuk before his own episode.

## Names that should never appear in the story (wiki-only)
- **Places and glosses:** Gwansanseong (관산성), Dokseongsanseong (독산성), Sinju (신주), Gucheon (구천), Buyeo Fortress, Bisa, the Thousand-Li Wall / Eastern Fortresses, Mamok Pass, Jungnyeong, Funan, Malgal country.
- **Kings by number:** Geunchogo (#13) and Gogukwon (#16), Jangsu (#20) and Gaero (#21), Seong (#26) and Jinheung (#24) as numbers, Sosurim, and "Yochang (later King Wideok)".
- **Peoples and dynasties as decoration:** Former Qin, Sogdian, Persians, Indian (in the Haesang list).
- **People who never matter:** princes Tae, Hyo and Yun; the commanders Son Daeha, Go Ul and Go Heumsong in narration (Yeon may still say them aloud).
- **System labels:** "Bone Rank System (골품제)", "Five Commanderies (오두)", "Ministers’ Assembly (정사암회의)", "Eight Great Clans (대성팔족)", "Gwanggaeto Stele (광개토대왕릉비)", "Taehak (태학)". Keep the concept and drop the parenthetical.
- **Technique jargon:** Sangdanse, satba, deulbaejigi (Eight Great Clans b6, b8, b9).
